chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa and Safwan and Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into Umrah and forgot to shorten his prayer until he entered into Hajj. He said: 'He seeks Allah's forgiveness and there is no penalty upon him, and his Umrah is complete.'
And it is appropriate for the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj) not to wear stitched clothing and to resemble the Muhrim (those in Ihram) when he shortens (his prayers).

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْعُمْرَةِ: Entered into the state of Ihram for Umrah
key_terms.اَلثِّيَابَ: Sitched clothing (as opposed to Ihram garments)
key_terms.دَخَلَ فِي اَلْحَجِّ: Entered into the state of Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.لِلْمُتَمَتِّعِ: For the Mutamatti' (one who combines Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَتَشَبَّهَ بِالْمُحْرِمِينَ: To resemble the Muhrim (those in Ihram)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten (the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shorten prayers during Umrah before starting Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who neglects to shorten prayers during Umrah al-Mufradah before entering Hajj Ihram, establishing that the Umrah remains valid with only Istighfar required, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in ritual obligations. It further prescribes that the Mutamatti' should avoid wearing stitched clothing to distinguish their state from the Ihram of the Hajj pilgrims, emphasizing the distinct legal statuses within the combined pilgrimage. This ruling underscores the jurisprudential nuance between the independent Umrah and the Hajj component in the Tammattu' mode.
